Which of these four is a physicist?
Ernest Lawrence is a physicist. A graduate of the University of South Dakota and University of Minnesota, Lawrence obtained a PhD in physics at Yale in 1925.
Who among these is a chemist?
Glenn T. Seaborg is a chemist. Throughout his career, Seaborg worked for arms control.
What is the atomic number of Boron?
Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.
In what year was Elon Musk born?
Elon Musk: Elon Reeve Musk (EE-lon; born June 28, 1971) is a businessman and former public official who is the CEO and largest shareholder of Tesla and SpaceX.
In what year was Radium discovered?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
In what year was Copper discovered?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.
Mil Mi-17: Kazan Helicopters. It is known as the Mi-8M series in Russian service.
In which country is Minamata disease?
Minamata disease: Japan. Minamata disease (Japanese: 水俣病, Hepburn: Minamata-byō) is a neurological disease caused by severe mercury poisoning.
Who is credited with discovering Thorium?
Thorium: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Thorium is a chemical element; it has symbol Th and atomic number 90.
Who is credited with discovering Cauchy–Schwarz inequality?
Cauchy–Schwarz inequality: Viktor Bunyakovsky. It is considered one of the most important and widely used inequalities in mathematics.
Who is credited with discovering Phosphorus?
Phosphorus: Hennig Brand. Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.
Formed by the angle of thyroid cartilage around the voice box, this neck protrusion becomes a prominent secondary sex characteristic in most men during puberty — what is it commonly called?
Adam's apple is the protrusion in the neck formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage surrounding the larynx, typically visible in men and less so in women.
Given by mouth, IV, or directly into bone marrow, which antiarrhythmic medication treats conditions like ventricular tachycardia but risks serious lung and thyroid side effects?
Amiodarone is an antiarrhythmic medication used to treat and prevent a number of types of cardiac dysrhythmias.
This emotion is defined by dread over events that haven't happened yet, distinguishing it from fear, which responds to a threat that's already present. What is it?
Anxiety is an emotion characterized by an unpleasant state of inner turmoil and includes feelings of dread over anticipated events.
These large Old World monkeys come in six distinct species, each native to a different region of Africa, with one species also found on the Arabian Peninsula — what primate is it?
Baboon are primates comprising the genus Papio, one of the 23 genera of Old World monkeys, in the family Cercopithecidae.
First coined in 1919 by Hungarian engineer Károly Ereky, this multidisciplinary field harnesses living organisms like bacteria and yeast to make products and services. What field is it?

Biotechnology is a multidisciplinary field that involves the integration of natural sciences and engineering sciences to achieve the application of organisms and parts thereof for products and services.

He won a share of the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physics for an effect he discovered in 1962 while still a Cambridge Ph.D. student — then later turned, controversially, to Transcendental Meditation. Which physicist is he?
Brian Josephson (born 4 January 1940) is a British theoretical physicist and emeritus professor at the University of Cambridge.
Bordered by Aquila, Sagittarius, and Aquarius in the sky's watery region, this half-goat, half-fish zodiac figure is the tiniest of the twelve — which constellation?
Capricornus is one of the constellations of the zodiac.
Known as garbanzo, chana or Bengal gram, this protein-rich legume is mashed into hummus and fried into falafel, with its oldest remains found in Syria — what is it?
Chickpea (Cicer arietinum) is an annual legume of the family Fabaceae, subfamily Faboideae, cultivated for its edible seeds.
More closely related to lungfish and land vertebrates than to ordinary ray-finned fish, this ancient lobe-finned fish survives today as a single genus with just two known species — which fish?
Coelacanth are an ancient group of lobe-finned fish (Sarcopterygii) in the class Actinistia.

This interdisciplinary field, whose name combines a Latin word for 'accusation' with a Greek suffix meaning 'study of,' draws on sociology, psychology, economics, and law to examine crime and deviant behavior. What field is this?
Criminology (from Latin crimen, 'accusation', and Ancient Greek -, -logia, from logos, 'word, reason') is the interdisciplinary study of crime and deviant behaviour.
This annual herb in the celery family, native to North Africa and West Asia, is grown across Eurasia for both its feathery leaves and its seeds, both used to flavor food — what herb is it?
Dill (Anethum graveolens) is an annual herb in the celery family Apiaceae.

Distinguished by permanently erect front fangs and a habit of rearing up while flaring a neck flap, which family of mostly venomous snakes ranges from an 18 cm white-lipped species to a nearly 6-metre giant?
Elapidae (commonly known as elapids, from Ancient) is a family of snakes characterized by their permanently erect fangs at the front of the mouth.

This genus of 700-plus flowering trees gets its name from Greek words meaning 'well covered' — a nod to the little cap fused over its stamens — and most species are native to Australia. The leafy 'gum trees' in question are which?
Eucalyptus is a genus of more than 700 species of flowering plants in the family Myrtaceae.
Found at the terminal end of the limb in many vertebrates, this weight-bearing anatomical structure enables locomotion and is typically made up of multiple bony segments — what is it?
Foot (pl.: feet) is an anatomical structure found in many vertebrates. The plural form feet is an instance of i-mutation.

Sometimes called the 'lesser apes' to distinguish them from chimpanzees, gorillas, and orangutans, these smaller, tailless primates live in forests from eastern Bangladesh through Southeast Asia and don't build nests — what are they?
Gibbon are apes in the family Hylobatidae (hylobatids).
This flatfish's English name blends words for 'holy' and 'flat fish,' a nod to its place on the Catholic holy-day menu. Which bottom-dwelling fish?
Halibut is the common name for three species of flatfish in the family of right-eye flounders.
Nesting monogamously in tree cavities across Africa, Asia, and Melanesia, these birds are unique for having their first two neck vertebrae fused solid — which birds?
Hornbill are birds found in tropical and subtropical Africa, Asia and Melanesia of the family Bucerotidae.

Co-creator of the breakthrough neural network AlexNet and a contributor to landmark AI systems including GPT and AlphaGo, this computer scientist has won a major deep-learning research award three years running — who is he?
Ilya Sutskever (born 1986) is a computer scientist who specializes in machine learning.
This American psychiatrist and Communist Party USA member is best remembered today for her romantic relationship with J. Robert Oppenheimer — who was she?
Jean Tatlock (February 21, 1914 - January 4, 1944) was an American psychiatrist.
Drawing on physiology, biomechanics, and neuropsychology, this scientific discipline studies human body movement and underpins fields from sports psychology to physical therapy — what is it?
Kinesiology (from Ancient Greek (knsis) 'movement' and - -loga 'study of') is the scientific study of human body movement.
This German-born American businessman founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans, launching his San Francisco firm in 1853 — who is he?
Levi Strauss (STROWSS; born Lb Strau,; February 26, 1829 - September 26, 1902) was a German-born American businessman who founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans.
The sole species in its genus, this South Chinese fruit has a sweet, mildly tart flavor and a distinctive rose-like floral aroma — name it?
Lychee (US also) are the fruit of the tree Litchi chinensis, the sole member of the genus Litchi, part of the soapberry family, Sapindaceae.
This genus of flowering plants belongs to the chamomile tribe of the sunflower family, and several of its species go by the folk name 'mayweed' — which genus?
Matricaria is a genus of flowering plants in the chamomile tribe within the sunflower family.
Touch this creeping legume's compound leaves and they fold inward within seconds, only reopening minutes later — a textbook example of rapid plant movement. What plant is it?

Mimosa pudica (also called sensitive plant, sleepy grass, sleepy plant, action plant, humble plant, touch-me-not, touch-and-die, shame plant or shy plant) is a creeping annual or perennial flowering plant of the pea/legume family Fabaceae.
Developed under a hypersonic flight program in the late 1990s, three single-use examples of this scramjet aircraft were built, the first destroyed in a 2001 test flight — which record holder is it?
NASA X-43 was an experimental unmanned hypersonic aircraft with multiple planned scale variations meant to test various aspects of hypersonic flight.
Built from proteins, DNA, and RNA around specific chromosomal regions, this nuclear structure is being studied as a target for cancer chemotherapy — what is it?
Nucleolus (pl.: nucleoli) is the largest structure in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
Founded as a science by Georges Cuvier in 1796, when he demonstrated evidence for extinction, this field studies prehistoric life mainly through fossils — what's the discipline?
Paleontology is the scientific study of the life of the past, mainly but not exclusively through the study of fossils.
Which management theorist and educator's writings on organizing business, government, and nonprofit sectors made him one of the most influential thinkers on modern management?

Peter Drucker (November 19, 1909 - November 11, 2005) was an Austrian American management consultant, educator, and author, whose writings contributed to the philosophical and practical foundations of modern management theory.
This genus of single-celled parasites moves from mosquito to human bloodstream, destroying red blood cells and causing a disease with recurring fevers — what is this genus called?
Plasmodium is a genus of unicellular eukaryotes that are obligate parasites of vertebrates and insects.
Classified into acute, chronic, and pelvic pain syndrome subtypes, this condition doesn't always match its name's literal meaning of organ swelling — which condition?
Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.

This bird of prey now breeds only in Europe, though it once also ranged across West Asia and Northwest Africa, with northern populations historically wintering as far as western Africa — what bird is it?
Red kite (Milvus milvus) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as eagles, buzzards, and harriers.
This root vegetable — a hybrid of cabbage and a related turnip-like plant — goes by different names in North America and Britain, and is often confused for a big turnip. What is it?
Rutabaga (North American English) or swede (British English and some Commonwealth English) is a root vegetable, a form of Brassica napus (which also includes rapeseed).
This Soviet rocket engineer led the early development of his country's space program and designed the R-7, the world's first intercontinental ballistic missile — who is he?
Sergei Korolev was Soviet aerospace engineer (1907–1966).

Barred from a formal education, she learned mathematics from her father's library and wrote to Gauss under the male pseudonym 'Monsieur Le Blanc,' later winning a Paris Academy prize for her work on elasticity. Which French mathematician was she?
Sophie Germain (1 April 1776 - 27 June 1831) was a French mathematician, physicist, and philosopher.
Developed from an earlier design, this variable-sweep-wing Soviet fighter-bomber served from 1967 to 1990 and was exported in variants like the Su-22 — which aircraft is it?
Sukhoi Su-17 (NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
A metabolite of caffeine processed in the liver, this bitter alkaloid is the main one in the cacao plant and turns up in chocolate, tea, and kola nuts. What is it?
Theobromine is the principal alkaloid of Theobroma cacao (cacao plant).
Formed from glycerol bonded to three fatty acids, these molecules make up the main constituents of body fat in humans and are also major components of human skin oil — what are they?
Triglyceride (from tri- and glyceride; also TG, triacylglycerol, TAG, or triacylglyceride) is an ester derived from glycerol and three fatty acids.
Its wild form is dioecious while domesticated versions bear hermaphrodite flowers — this Mediterranean-native plant is the ancestor of nearly all wine and table varieties — what species?

Vitis vinifera is a species of flowering plant, native to the Mediterranean region, Central Europe, and southwestern Asia, from Morocco and Portugal north to southern Germany and east to northern Iran.
Which East Asian citrus fruit, believed to have originated in central China as a hybrid of mandarin orange and ichang papeda, is now also grown in New Zealand, Australia, and parts of Europe?
Yuzu (Citrus junos, from Japanese or) is a citrus fruit and plant in the family Rutaceae of Chinese origin.
Nicknamed the 'upside-down tree' for its unusual silhouette, this genus of long-lived African and Malagasy giants was named after a French naturalist — what genus is it?
Adansonia: Genus of trees known as baobab.
Made in the adrenal cortex, this hormone tells the kidney to hang onto sodium and dump potassium, quietly steering your blood pressure and blood volume — what is it?
Formed when ammonia gains an extra hydrogen ion, this positively charged molecule, NH4+, is a key player in the global nitrogen cycle — what is it?
This scientific practice of systematically measuring the human body has been used in paleoanthropology, historical living-standards research, and modern clothing design — what is it called?
Anthropometry: Measurement of the human individual.

This umbrella term for joint disease covers conditions like osteoarthritis, most common in weight-bearing joints as people age, and the autoimmune form that typically targets the hands and feet. What condition is this?
Best known for pioneering radical behaviorism at Harvard, this psychologist invented a chamber for studying operant conditioning that came to bear his name — who is he?
B. F. Skinner: American psychologist and social philosopher (1904–1990)
Originating in the Swiss Alps' canton of Bern, this large farm breed historically pulled carts for alpine herders and traces its ancestry to Roman mastiffs — which breed, recognized in 1912?
Bernese Mountain Dog: Swiss breed of dog. The Bernese Mountain Dog, German: Berner Sennenhund or Dürrbächler, is a large dog breed originating from the canton of Bern, Switzerland and the Swiss Alps.
The only trijet ever produced by its manufacturer, this airliner entered service with Eastern Air Lines in 1964 powered by three rear-mounted turbofans?
A tree-like cluster of dark-green flower heads sprouting from a thick pale stalk, this cabbage-family vegetable is a close cousin of cauliflower and can be eaten raw or cooked — what is it?
Broccoli: Edible green plant in the cabbage family.
Named to honor the Virgin Mary and her golden crown, this daisy-family flower is also known as the pot marigold — which plant?
Calendula officinalis: Species of flowering plant in the daisy family Asteraceae.
Known also as yoke elm, this species of hornbeam native to Western Asia and Europe grows only up to elevations of about 1,000 metres — which species?
Carpinus betulus: Species of tree. It requires a warm climate for good growth, and occurs only at elevations up to 1,000 metres (3,300 ft).

Serving as royal executioner under Louis XVI and later chief executioner of the First Republic, this Frenchman carried out nearly 3,000 executions during his 40-year career, including those of the king, queen, and Robespierre — who is he?

Also bearing the names Krebs and TCA, this loop of biochemical reactions unlocks the energy in nutrients via the oxidation of acetyl-CoA — and is thought to be one of the earliest metabolic components. What is it?
Citric acid cycle: Interconnected biochemical reactions releasing energy.
This icy wanderer of the solar system grows a gassy halo and sometimes a tail stretching more than an astronomical unit as it nears the sun — what is it?
Comet: Natural object in space that releases gas.
Spread mainly through the fecal-oral route, these single-stranded RNA enteroviruses share traits with poliovirus and rank among the leading causes of aseptic meningitis — which pathogens?
Coxsackievirus: Virus that causes digestive upset and sometimes heart damage.
This Harvard-trained legal scholar who wrote on criminal punishment and retribution joined Florida State's faculty in 2005, and was later murdered in a plot tied to his ex-wife's family — who is he?
Dan Markel: American law professor and murder victim (1972–2014)
This colorless, highly flammable liquid with a sweet smell was once widely used as a general anesthetic before modern alternatives — what compound?
After co-founding a social media giant, this entrepreneur left in 2008 to launch the workplace software company Asana — who is he?
Nicknamed the ALX, this Brazilian turboprop light-attack aircraft is assembled in Jacksonville, Florida with an American defense partner for low-threat counter-insurgency missions — which aircraft?
Embraer EMB 314 Super Tucano: Light ground attack and training aircraft.
Odorless, colorless, and dangerously sweet-tasting, this viscous compound goes into polyester fibers and antifreeze — and has even been spotted in outer space. What is it?
Born in 1963, this woman is the daughter of the last Shah of Iran by his third wife — who is she?
Sold under the brand name Prozac, this SSRI treats depression, OCD and panic disorder, and is also prescribed off-label for premature ejaculation — what is it?
Fluoxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It is also approved for treatment of major depressive disorder in adolescents and children 8 years of age and over.
With a melting point of just under 30 degrees Celsius, this metal will turn to liquid in the palm of your hand — which element?
Gallium: Chemical element with atomic number 31 (Ga)
Found in birds, crocodilians, and earthworms alike, this thick-muscled digestive organ grinds food with the help of swallowed grit — what's it called?
Gizzard: Digestive organ of some animals.

This algebraic structure — a set paired with an operation that's associative, has an identity element, and gives every member an inverse — is exemplified by the integers under addition. What is it called?

Group (mathematics): Set with associative invertible operation. The concept of a group was elaborated for handling, in a unified way, many mathematical structures such as numbers, geometric shapes and polynomial roots.

Often defined as the normal functioning of the body free of disease, pain, or injury, this multidimensional state of well-being can be promoted by exercise and sleep and harmed by smoking or stress — what's the one-word concept?
Health: Desirable level of functional or metabolic efficiency of a living being.
Named for the English physician who first described it in 1832, this cancer is defined by multinucleated Reed–Sternberg cells in the lymph nodes — what is it?
Hodgkin lymphoma: Type of blood and immune-system cancer.
This immune response causes tissue damage upon repeated exposure to an antigen and underlies conditions like hay fever, which affects roughly one in ten people worldwide — what is it called?
Hypersensitivity: Overreaction of the immune system to an antigen.
This sugar alcohol, with about half the sweetness of table sugar, is made by the human kidney at roughly two grams a day and reaches its highest concentration in the brain — what is it?
Inositol: Carbocyclic sugar. Its formula is C6H12O6; the molecule has a ring of six carbon atoms, each with a hydrogen atom and a hydroxy group (–OH).
Often mislabeled 'yellowtail tuna' on sushi menus, this northwest Pacific jack fish is unrelated to true tuna and is called hamachi when served as sashimi — which species?
Japanese amberjack: Species of fish. The Japanese amberjack or yellowtail, Seriola quinqueradiata, is a species of jack fish in the family Carangidae, native to the northwest Pacific Ocean.
Also called the red date or Chinese date, this buckthorn-family fruit is eaten fresh, dried, or candied — what is it?
Jujube: Species of plant with edible fruit.
This severe form of childhood protein malnutrition causes swelling and an enlarged, fatty liver, and is distinct from the calorie-deficient condition known as marasmus — what is it?
Kwashiorkor: Severe protein malnutrition. Kwashiorkor ( KWOSH-ee-OR-kor, -⁠kər) is a form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema and an enlarged liver with fatty infiltrates.
Sold under the brand name Xyzal, this less-sedating second-generation antihistamine for hay fever and hives was patented in 1965 but not approved in the US until 2007 — what is it?
Levocetirizine: Antihistamine medication. It is classified as a second-generation antihistamine and works by blocking histamine H1-receptors.
Nicknamed the sea devil, frogfish, or fishing frog, this species anchors a major commercial fishery in the Irish Sea and ranges from the Barents Sea to the Mediterranean — which fish?
Lophius piscatorius: Species of fish. Lophius piscatorius, commonly known as the angler, toadfish, sea frog, fishing frog, frogfish, or sea devil, is a species of Lophius in the family Lophiidae.
Males of this widespread dabbling duck species sport iridescent green heads, while females have brown-speckled plumage — which bird?
Mallard: Species of duck. The mallard or wild duck (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.
Distinguished by its darker camouflage, conformal fuel tanks, and a two-seat cockpit, this all-weather multirole fighter first flew in 1986 for long-range interdiction missions — what is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle: American all-weather multirole fighter aircraft.
First made in 1969 and approved for medical use in 1978, this selective beta blocker treats high blood pressure, angina, and helps prevent migraines — what is it called?
Metoprolol: Beta blocker medication. It is also used to prevent further heart problems after myocardial infarction and to prevent headaches in those with migraines.
With velvety fur, tiny eyes, and powerful digging forelimbs, this subterranean mammal aerates garden soil and feasts on earthworms and slugs despite being seen as a pest — what is it?
Mole (animal): Common name for several small mammals.
One of the smallest self-replicating organisms known, this cell-wall-lacking bacterium was originally called the 'Eaton agent' after being cultivated in chicken eggs in 1944 — what organism is it?
Mycoplasma pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a species of very small-cell bacteria that lack a cell wall, in the class Mollicutes.
This semiaquatic salamander's juvenile phase is nicknamed an 'eft,' and adults return to the water every year to breed after living mostly on land — what is it?
Newt: Salamander in the subfamily Pleurodelinae.
Weighing up to 1,000 kg and resembling a fish head without a tail, this giant marine creature can be as tall as it is long when its fins are extended — what is it?
Ocean sunfish: Species of fish. The ocean sunfish (Mola mola), also known as the common mola, is one of the largest bony fish in the world.
This genus of highly sociable ruminants includes domestic sheep, believed to descend from the wild mouflon of central and southwest Asia — which genus?
Ovis: Genus of mammals. Ovis is a genus of mammals, part of the Caprinae subfamily of the ruminant family Bovidae.
One of the 20th century's most prolific mathematicians, this Hungarian championed Ramsey theory and famously preferred cracking open problems to building grand theories — who was he?
Found naturally in mammals' milk and a direct precursor to phenethylamine, this is one of nine amino acids your body can't make, so you eat it in meat, eggs, and legumes — which one?

There are exactly five of these convex regular polyhedra — tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron — named for the philosopher who linked them to the classical elements. What are they called?
Platonic solid: Any of the five regular polyhedra. In geometry, a Platonic solid is a convex, regular polyhedron in three-dimensional Euclidean space.

A trained engineer by profession, this royal consort married King Mohammed VI in 2002, becoming the first publicly acknowledged wife of a reigning monarch there to hold an official title, before their discreet 2018 divorce. Who is she?
Princess Lalla Salma of Morocco: Moroccan royal (born 1978)
Imagine a benzene ring with one CH swapped for a nitrogen atom: the result is this flammable, fish-smelling liquid once distilled from coal tar and now made at 20,000 tons a year — what is it?
Known in North America as caribou, this circumpolar deer species ranges from the tiny Svalbard subspecies to the much larger Osborn's version roaming the Arctic tundra — which animal is it?
Reindeer: Species of deer. It is the only representative of the genus Rangifer.

This chronic skin condition causes facial redness, small dilated blood vessels, and in severe cases an enlarged red nose, and can be triggered by spicy food, alcohol, or sun exposure — which condition?
Rosacea: Skin condition, usually on the face.
Nicknamed 'mother-in-law's tongue' and 'snake plant,' this genus of stiff, sword-leaved succulents from Africa and southern Asia is now classified within Dracaena — which genus?
Serving as mayor of Moscow since 2010, this Russian politician previously headed the presidential administration and served as a deputy prime minister under Vladimir Putin — who is he?
Sergey Sobyanin: Mayor of Moscow since 2010. At the same time, Sobyanin was criticized for the banning of pride parades in the city, for which he was strongly condemned by LGBT groups.
Coined in the late 18th century, this social science studies human society — from one-on-one interactions to sweeping social structures and everyday culture. What is it?
Sociology: Scientific study of human society and relationships.
This Polish-American mathematician on the Manhattan Project dreamed up the cellular automaton and the Monte Carlo method, and co-designed the thermonuclear bomb — who was he?
Stanisław Ulam: Polish mathematician and physicist (1909–1984)
This medical specialty uses manual and instrumental techniques to treat disease, reshape the body, or remove diseased tissue, performed by a lead practitioner and an assistant?
Surgery: Medical procedures that involve incisive or invasive instruments into body cavities.
This cloud-based messaging service, known for large group chats and channels, launched on iOS in August of which year?
Telegram launched for iOS on 14 August 2013 and for Android on 20 October 2013, allowing users to exchange messages, share files and hold voice or video calls.
This blood-feeding arachnid's oldest fossils date back roughly 100 million years to the Cretaceous, and it comes in two main flavors: hard-bodied and soft-bodied — which parasite?
Tick: Order of arachnids in the arthropod phylum.

This genetic disorder causes small body size, heart defects, clenched fists with overlapping fingers, and severe intellectual disability, with risk rising alongside maternal age. What's the condition?
Trisomy 18: Chromosomal disorder in which there are three copies of chromosome 18.
Native to Europe and southwestern Asia, this herbaceous perennial is the type species that lends its name to an entire genus of flowering plants — what is it?
Valerian (herb): Species of flowering plant. Valerian (Valeriana officinalis) is an herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the family Caprifoliaceae, native to Europe and southwestern Asia.
Denoted by the Greek letter lambda, this measure of a repeating wave's spatial period shrinks as frequency rises for a wave moving at constant speed — what is it called?
Wavelength: Distance over which a wave's shape repeats.
Native to South America and first cultivated by the Guaraní people, the steeped leaves of this holly-genus plant produce a caffeinated beverage — what is it?
Yerba mate: South American holly plant. Yerba mate or yerba maté ( YUR-bə MAH-tay), Ilex paraguariensis, is a plant species of the holly genus native to South America.
The symbol for tungsten is W. Tungsten is a chemical element; it has symbol W and atomic number 74.
The symbol for platinum is Pt. Platinum is a chemical element; it has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.

In what year was Steve McQueen born?

Jessica Alba: Jessica Marie Alba ( AL-bə; born April 28, 1981) is an American actress and businesswoman.

Howard Hughes: Howard Robard Hughes Jr. (December 24, 1905 – April 5, 1976) was an American aviator, aerospace engineer, business magnate, film producer, and investor.
In what year did Alfred Hitchcock die?
Alfred Hitchcock: Sir Alfred Joseph Hitchcock (13 August 1899 – 29 April 1980) was an English filmmaker.
In what year was Apollo 13 first released?
